sections.h2: Which ways of selling a house fast fit a Bartlett owner?
sections.html:
Bartlett owners can choose an agent listing, a sale by owner, or an as-is cash purchase. A cash sale skips buyer financing and appraisal steps, which is where speed comes from, while a listing may bring more money for a house in good shape.

  • Agent listing: highest potential price, but repairs, showings and a lender's timeline come with it.
  • By owner: you keep the commission and take on pricing, contracts and disclosure yourself.
  • Cash purchase: sold as-is on a short timeline, with no repairs or showings.

Each route ends the same way in Bartlett and Shelby County: a city code check, a tax payoff and a deed filed with the Shelby County Register.

Bartlett is a city in Shelby County, Tennessee, with a mayor and council form of government and David Parsons as mayor. The city covers about 32 square miles and is the 14th most populous city in Tennessee.

The town began as a stagecoach stop called Union Depot on the westward route from Nashville, then became a railroad station. It was incorporated on November 1, 1866 and was named for Major Gabriel M. Bartlett, a planter and early settler. Growth came late. The 1970 census counted 1,150 people, and by 1980 the figure was 17,170, followed by 40,543 in 2000 and 54,613 in 2010.

Landmarks include the Bartlett Performing Arts and Conference Center, which opened in 1999 and held Art Garfunkel as its first show, and the Nicholas Gotten House of 1871, which now holds the Bartlett Museum. Bartlett City Schools runs the public schools. Voters approved the district on July 16, 2013, and it opened in fall 2014 with the 11 school buildings inside the city limits.

sections.h2: How is the Bartlett housing market for sellers?
sections.html:
Few cities in this part of Tennessee have a higher share of owners. Census figures for 2020 to 2024 put the median owned home at $310,400 and owner occupancy at 85.6 percent.

  • Median household income: $102,070, with 5.1 percent of residents in poverty.
  • Households: 20,051, averaging 2.80 people.
  • Median gross rent: $1,638, with monthly owner costs of $1,775 with a mortgage and $639 without.
  • Population: 56,416 on July 1, 2025, down 2.4 percent from the 57,792 estimates base in April 2020.
  • Average commute: 24.4 minutes each way for workers 16 and older.
  • Same house one year earlier: 91.4 percent of residents.

Population density is 1,790 people per square mile on 32.28 square miles of land. With a stable resident base and a slightly smaller population than in 2020, expect buyers to compare condition and price closely.

sections.h2: What does Bartlett code enforcement check before a house sale?
sections.html:
Bartlett's Code Compliance department checks sidewalks and storm inlets when it is told a house is for sale. The city's page says staff mark any sidewalk or inlet in need of replacement or repair.

The Code Enforcement Department at 6382 Stage Road, 901-385-6425, handles permits, plan review and inspections Monday through Friday, 8 to 5, and also performs MLGW service turn-on inspections. Permits are required for fences, decks, detached buildings, swimming pools of 24 inches or deeper, additions, siding, window replacement, concrete patios and driveway extensions. Water heater, HVAC and electrical work must be pulled by a licensed contractor.

Sellers should check older unpermitted work before a buyer's inspector finds it. Call the department to learn whether a permit exists on file for your fence, deck or addition.

sections.h2: How are Bartlett house taxes billed?
sections.html:
A Bartlett owner receives a city tax bill and a Shelby County tax bill. The City of Bartlett mails its bills before December 1, payable through February 28, and taxes become delinquent on March 1. Prior years' city taxes are collected by Shelby County.

sections.h2: Who handles tax questions for Bartlett properties?
sections.html:
Appraisal changes and ownership updates come from the Shelby County Assessor, at 1075 Mullins Station Road in Memphis, 901-222-7001. The Shelby County Trustee at 157 Poplar Ave., 901-222-0200, collects the county tax and can take delinquent city tax payments on weekdays until 4:30 p.m..

Shelby County offers some payment flexibility. A Quarterly Pay program lets qualifying owners 65 or older on a fixed income pay county tax on October 31, January 31, April 30 and July 31. Call 901-222-0200 for the current application window. The trustee also accepts partial payments, with no interest if the bill is paid in full by the deadline, and it offers ManagedPay monthly plans, though ManagedPay does not stop interest from accruing. Per Bartlett's FAQ, the Shelby County Trustee supplies city tax relief and tax freeze forms for older owners.

sections.h2: Where is a Bartlett deed filed, and what does it need?
sections.html:
Deeds for Bartlett houses are recorded with the Shelby County Register of Deeds, whose main office is at 1075 Mullins Station Road, Building W-3, Memphis, TN 38134. The Register says recording takes about one business day from receipt, and a digital copy appears on its website.

A taxable deed must identify grantor and grantee and include an affidavit of value, a derivation clause, the property address, who owns the parcel and who answers for its taxes, the ward, block and parcel number, the preparer's contact details, and a valid acknowledgment. Taxable deeds pay $0.37 per $100. At Bartlett's $310,400 median value that comes to about $1,148, before the page fee. Deeds between divorcing spouses, deeds that carry out a will, and transfers into or out of a revocable living trust are exempt under T.C.A. 67-4-409.

faqs.q: How quickly can a Bartlett house be sold?
faqs.a: If title is clear, a cash sale can close within days. A listing depends on the buyer's lender, and the Shelby County Register reports about one business day to record a deed.

faqs.q: Does Bartlett inspect a house before it is sold?
faqs.a: Bartlett's Code Compliance department checks and marks sidewalks and storm inlets needing repair when it is notified of a house for sale. Call Code Enforcement at 901-385-6425 to ask what applies to your lot.

faqs.q: When are Bartlett city property taxes due?
faqs.a: City bills are mailed before December 1 and are payable through February 28, with delinquency starting March 1. Prior year city taxes are collected by Shelby County.

faqs.q: What transfer tax will I pay when I sell in Bartlett?
faqs.a: Tennessee's transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of price or value, whichever is greater, and the Shelby County Register collects it with the deed. A $100,000 price means $370.
